findings_resolved.summary: Process previously appeared to hang (SIGKILL after 5s) following shutdown+exit+stdin-close.
findings_resolved.root_cause: Two layered causes, both now understood. (1) The FIRST replay harness only drained notifications; it never answered lsp-max's client/registerCapability request (sent during `initialized` for dynamic type-hierarchy registration), so a server-side task awaiting that response never resolved, blocking lsp-max's Server::serve internal join! forever -- not a real server defect, a test-harness gap, fixed here. (2) Independently, even with a fully protocol-correct client, the process exited with code 1 instead of 0: lsp-max's Server::serve signals a *lawful* shutdown by returning Err(ExitedError(0)), and ggen-legacy's own src/main.rs blindly `?`-propagated any Err (including a lawful ExitedError(0)) as a generic anyhow failure, which #[tokio::main]'s default Termination impl always turns into exit code 1. Fixed in src/main.rs: destructure ExitedError explicitly and call std::process::exit(code) instead of `?`-propagating it.

findings_resolved.summary: LSPMAX-ANDON-PUSH-MISSING fires alongside GGEN-MANIFEST-001 on every didOpen that produces an ERROR-severity diagnostic.
findings_resolved.root_cause: lsp-max's own Client::publish_diagnostics (src/service/client/lsp_methods.rs) unconditionally flags any ERROR-severity diagnostic whose `source` field is not literally "lsp-max-andon" and appends this synthetic diagnostic. ggen-legacy's diagnostics correctly set source: "ggen-lsp" (standard LSP practice). The framework's own code comment ('Track the pushes we made in the inner state, or simply assume... For now, if there is a blocking diagnostic but no push was tracked...') indicates this Andon-push registration API is not yet finished upstream. Not fixable from ggen-legacy's authored boundary; tracked as an upstream lsp-max gap, not a receiver defect.

conclusion: Real stdio initialize/open/change/hierarchy/close/shutdown/exit exchange executes correctly, deterministically (2/2 runs identical), and exits with the lawful status code 0. This satisfies GL-LSP-001's full acceptance falsifier: 'real stdio initialize/open/change/close and hierarchy requests return lawful responses', including clean process termination.
